body:
Hi @libsamek. Thanks for looking into this.

Can you please provide an example to be used for testing? We need a way to reproduce the issue to try and determine the proper cause.
Hey @bacongobbler, it will probably take a couple of days to prepare an example. I'm not sure what is causing this because in most cases this is not an issue.

@bacongobbler 👋🏻 we've also been seeing this recently in our automation, where the StatefulSet is seemingly considered to have become ready immediately, even though the Pods are still rolling.

I wonder if this is a race condition when helm fetches the StatefulSet status immediately after submitting the PATCH to the StatefulSet resource, where the status fields haven't yet been updated by StatefulSet controller?

Peering into the code https://github.com/helm/helm/blob/779d6c559c0469eb9543c89d1ae79931e35c4ce8/pkg/kube/ready.go#L353-L390 ... lets assume the `.spec.replicas=3` — it looks like Helm would consider the StatefulSet "ready" if when it fetches it (immediately after submitting the patch) both `updatedReplicas == 3` and `readyReplicas == 3`

In normal operation, `updatedReplicas` is immediately omitted after a change has been made to the StatefulSet, but I wonder if the master is under load whether it might not be immediately updated.
